title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 41-43). 𝔖^+ is a group generated by ρ, σ with ω = σ² central. It contains a commutative normal subgroup M generated by λ₀ = ω·σρσρ and λ₁ = ω·ρσρσ (with a λ_∞ in the same family). Elsewhere there is a 'linearised' version M̲, an S₀-group (scheme) with group of sections ΓM̲. Grothendieck wants an automorphism u of the group 𝔖^+ (pushed out along M→M̲) given by the twisted formulas (33): u(ρ) = ξρ and u(σ) = ω^{ν₂}η₀σ. Here ξ = α₀ − ρ(α₀) + ν₃λ₁ and η₀ = β₀ − σ(β₀) lie in ΓM̲, so they are coboundaries corrected by a central or M-term. On this page he computes the effect of u on M.

(i) u(ω) = ω (37). We have u(σ²) = (η₀σ)(η₀σ) = η₀·σ(η₀)·σ². Here η₀·σ(η₀) = (1+σ)(1−σ)β₀ = (1−σ²)β₀ = 0, because ω = σ² acts trivially on M. The power ω^{ν₂} squares to 1.

(ii) The previous page gives u(l₀) = l₀^{(μ)} with μ = 2ν+1 = 4ν′+2ν₂+1. Hence u(λ₀) = u(ω)u(l₀) = ω·l₀^{μ} = λ₀·l₀^{2ν} = λ₀^{μ}. This uses ω central with ω² = 1, so that l₀^{2ν} = λ₀^{2ν}.

(iii) λ₁ = int(ρ)(λ₀) and u∘int(ρ) = int(u(ρ))∘u = int(ξρ)∘u = int(ρ)∘u on M, since ξ ∈ M and M is commutative. So u(λ₁) = λ₁^{μ}. Conclusion (38): u acts on M (hence on M̲) as multiplication by the odd 'scalar' μ, and similarly on λ_∞. This is the expected shape: an automorphism of an extension of a 'modular-type' group by an abelian kernel, acting on the kernel through a character μ, analogous to a cyclotomic-type character.

(iv) Grothendieck then remarks that these computations are 'vaseux' (logically muddy). The verification has tacitly been done in a bigger group, a free group on ρ, σ, …, while the existence of u is still unproved. To make it rigorous he invokes the intrinsic description (39): 𝔖^+ = 𝔖^+_{S₀} ∧^{M_{S₀}} M̲_{S₀}, the pushout of the extension along M → M̲. A homomorphism from 𝔖^+ to an S₀-group G is then given by a pair (u_M̲, u_𝔖) satisfying two conditions (next page): they agree on M, and u_M̲ is equivariant for the conjugation actions. He applies this with u_M̲(λ) = i(μλ). This is the standard universal property of the Baer pushout of a group extension with abelian kernel.
errors: Grothendieck himself flags that the derivation is not rigorous. It presupposes that u is already a well-defined homomorphism, and the computations take place in a larger free group. The fix via the pushout universal property is only begun.
'la deuxième formule (3)' should be (33); a slip in reference numbering.

The step η₀σ(η₀) = 1 requires that ω = σ² act trivially on M. This holds only if M is not, e.g., the standard Z² lattice on which −1 ∈ SL₂ acts by −1. It is implicitly assumed and not stated on this page.

ideas.what: Automorphism of a group extension of a ρ,σ-generated group by an abelian kernel, defined by coboundary-twisted images of generators and acting on the kernel by an odd scalar μ
ideas.modern_name: Automorphisms of extensions / character twist (cyclotomic-type action) on an abelian normal subgroup
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical group cohomology of extensions; in the anabelian setting Grothendieck, Ihara, Drinfeld and others
ideas.where_published: Thematically close to La Longue Marche (1981), unpublished; not known in this exact form

ideas.what: Defining homomorphisms out of a pushout extension 𝔖^+ ∧^M M̲ via compatible pairs (agreement on M plus equivariance)
ideas.modern_name: Universal property of the Baer pushout of a group extension along an equivariant map of the abelian kernel
ideas.where_published: Analogous constructions (contracted products) appear in SGA 7 and SGA 3 style; unsure of exact place

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine verification inside a longer computation of automorphisms of a Teichmüller/modular-type extension. The scalar action on the abelian kernel and the pushout universal property are standard. Nothing is new beyond private working details.
transcription_corrections: '(∫ρ u)(λ₀)' and '(∫ρ)' should read 'int(ρ)' (inner automorphism by ρ): u(λ₁) = u(int(ρ)(λ₀)) = (int(ρ)∘u)(λ₀) = int(ρ)(u(λ₀)) = int(ρ)(λ₀^μ) = λ₁^μ.
'u(σ) = (β₀ − σ(β₀))ω^{1/2}.σ' is likely 'ω^{ν₂}.σ', consistent with (33) and (36).
'la deuxième formule (3)' in the image refers to formula (33).
The marginal note reads 'i.e. μ = 2ν+1 = 4ν′ + 2ν₂ + 1' next to (38), consistent with the previous page.
'𝔲(ε₀²)' is just u(ε₀²); the fraktur is likely an artefact.
On the last lines, read 'un groupe libre engendré par ρ, σ, …' with 'caractéristique' inserted above (possibly 'groupe libre caractéristique').
'homomorphisme' (definir un homomorphisme de 𝔖^+ dans un S₀-groupe G) matches the image's 'homom'.
